one_line: Sultan of Bijapur who oversaw the vast Gol Gumbaz and ruled a Deccan court famed for its artists, astrologers and chroniclers.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s to early 40s, medium height with a solid, slightly broad build suggesting a ruler used to court life rather than battlefield hardship
appearance.face: Oval face with a neatly trimmed black beard and moustache, warm medium-brown complexion, straight nose, slightly heavy-lidded large anime-style eyes with a calm, contemplative gaze; default expression is composed and dignified, with a hint of introspective melancholy.
appearance.hair: Hair mostly hidden under a tall Deccan-style turban: layered, slightly conical white muslin turban wrapped over a soft cap, with a narrow golden band at the base and a single dark green plume pinned at the front; a few short black sideburns visible in front of the ears.
appearance.costume: He wears an early-17th-century Deccan court jama in fine cotton: a long, overlapping, calf-length robe that fastens slightly off-center to the right, in muted teal with delicate pale-gold buta (paisley-like) motifs, full sleeves tapering at the wrists; over this, a sleeveless, waist-length quilted silk coat (nimcha) in deep maroon with subtle vertical stitching and a thin gold edging; at the waist, a broad cream-and-gold striped sash tightly wrapped and knotted slightly to the side, from which hangs a small dagger sheath; loose churidar trousers in soft off-white cotton gather in slight folds at the ankles; his feet are in pointed Deccani leather shoes (mojari) in dark brown with a slight upturned toe and simple stitched decoration; minimal jewellery: a single string of off-white pearls close to the neck, a narrow gold bracelet on the right wrist, and a simple gold ring on one hand, keeping the overall look regal yet restrained and historically grounded.
appearance.signature: A single, gently curved Deccan talwar with a slightly broad blade, worn sheathed at his left side: the hilt has a disc-shaped pommel and cross-guard of dark steel with subtle gold koftgari inlay, the wooden scabbard covered in deep-brown leather with a thin brass chape.

ref_desc: Muhammad Adil Shah is a medium-built, bearded Deccan sultan in a muted teal patterned jama with a maroon quilted waistcoat, cream sash, off-white churidar, dark brown shoes, a white conical turban with green plume, and a sheathed curved talwar at his side.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Muhammad Adil Shah of Bijapur: a medium-built man in his late 30s to early 40s with an oval face, warm medium-brown skin, large calm eyes, and a neatly trimmed black beard and moustache. His hair is mostly hidden under a tall Deccan white turban wrapped in layered muslin over a soft cap, slightly conical, with a narrow golden band at the base and a single dark green feather plume pinned at the front, and short black sideburns visible. He wears a long, overlapping calf-length jama robe in muted teal cotton with delicate pale-gold buta motifs, fastening slightly off-center to the right, the full sleeves tapering at the wrists. Over this is a sleeveless, waist-length quilted silk coat in deep maroon with subtle vertical stitching and a thin gold edging. A broad cream-and-gold striped sash wraps tightly around his waist and is knotted slightly to one side, with a small dagger sheath hanging from it. His loose churidar trousers are off-white cotton, gathered in soft folds at the ankles, and his feet are in dark brown pointed Deccani leather shoes with slightly upturned toes and simple stitched decoration. He wears modest jewellery: a single short strand of off-white pearls around his neck, a narrow gold bracelet on his right wrist, and a simple gold ring. At his left side is his signature weapon, a gently curved Deccan talwar worn sheathed: disc-shaped pommel and cross-guard in dark steel with subtle gold inlay, and a deep-brown leather-covered scabbard with a slim brass chape. Use a palette dominated by muted teal, deep maroon, cream, off-white and dark brown, and present him in neutral, rotation-friendly poses that clearly show his face, turban, layered garments and the sheathed talwar.
